title: Squirrel and Mole
text: It took me a while to realize they were even hiding their distinctive tail. After all, squirrel-type demi-humans exist in places like Siltvelt too, so it wasn't as if it were a given. Well, that distinctive Santa hat made it easy enough to pick them out, though. Their eyes seemed to have grown a lot sharper too, I'd say.
“You are—…?”

Father stared at Itsuki-turned-riska as if he had no idea who this was. But then his gaze drifted to the Santa hat perched atop Itsuki's head, now that the hood was off. He was probably drawing a connection from the Santa hat he'd seen earlier on Ren's head.
“I suppose you wouldn't recognize me like this. Me, reduced to such a form… Fufu, go ahead and laugh if you want to. But more importantly—”
Itsuki said this with a hint of self-mockery, then turned his gaze toward Mole.
“Hmm? Are you after Imiya? No can do.”

Kou shifted his stance to shield Mole, tucking her behind his back. Itsuki frowned slightly at that, but quickly turned his attention back to Father. Meanwhile, Father, along with Éclair and Crocodile Guy, all had their eyes fixed on the Santa hat atop Itsuki's head.
“Ah…”
“Hmm… Iwatani-dono.”
“Yeah. Right. Mind if I just ask you straight out?”
“Sure, I'd appreciate it if you'd just say whatever's on your mind. We've got plenty going on over here too.”
“Alright then… you're Itsuki, right? Itsuki Kawasumi, to use your full name?”
Itsuki's eyes went wide at Father's question. He was probably about to deny it. Itsuki, so obsessed with justice, always lied at times like this.
“How did you know? Me, reduced to such a wretched form… is this some special ability of the Shield Hero's?”
“It's nothing like that. I'm guessing something happened to you too, but we've had our own share of stuff going on…”
Itsuki's eyes welled up with tears that seemed mixed with both joy and sorrow. Just then, a faint noise came from the direction of Mole's burrow.
“It's alright. These are people I know, and there's no problem with them. Please, come out.”

Itsuki wiped away his tears and called out loudly. Then, from the burrow… out came a mole and Stalker Pig. Mole—the one Kou had been carrying on his back—caught sight of the mole emerging warily and hesitantly from the burrow, and let out a cry of surprise. Reading the mood, Kou set Mole down.
“Emia-san!?”
“Someone of the same species as Imiya-chan.”
Mole rushed toward the mole who had come out of the burrow, embracing her as though overjoyed at their reunion.
“Oink…”
Stalker Pig was, for some reason, dressed in something like a maid outfit. Total character overlap with Takt's maid pig, I say.
“Imiya-chan, who's that?”
“Oh, right. This is… Emia Nirwen Risera Tereti Kuarizu. She's my older cousin.”

As terrifyingly long a name as ever. What's more, it's off by only one syllable from Mole's own name, so I very nearly misheard it entirely. Impressive that anyone remembers it. I'd already forgotten it myself. That's the sort of name that goes in one ear and straight out the other. Names ought to be simpler—easy to remember, like Filo-tan's. Like Yuki-chan, Kuro-chan, Kou, or Sakura-chan. There are far too many people in this world with names ending in -ria or -mia. Apparently, by this world's standards, -ria and -mia carry special meanings mixed in, like benevolence or bravery. Sort of like how Father's name, Naofumi, apparently means something about revering the written word. Surely it has nothing to do with the adorable sound of a kitten going “nya~o” or the way one kneads its bedding with “fumi fumi,” of all things. In my mind's eye I could picture Ark striking a beckoning-cat pose with a delighted expression he'd never actually wear in real life—but no, surely that's not it either. Incidentally, Father mentioned that in a different loop, he'd once been given the nickname “Nyao-fumi,” or called a “cat-type boy.” Oh? The Father from the very first world was cracking his knuckles with a distinctly displeased look on his face. As if to say, what on earth are you thinking about at a time like this. Surely, it was just my imagination.
“U-um, I see.”
Father answered, looking troubled. Understandable, given how absurdly long the name was. Come to think of it, Big Sister was always good at remembering people's names.
“I just call her Emia-san. And this is… Rishia-san.”
“Oink oink… oink.”
Stalker Pig's reply sounded rather listless. A little fearful, it seemed.
“I—I see. So then… where should we start?”

“There's a great deal we need to discuss, but first, Naofumi-san. Motoyasu-san seems to be here as well—why have you come to a place like this? We may be acquainted, but depending on your answer, I won't hold back.”
“Ha! You may sound like Itsuki, but whether or not you hold back means nothing to me, I say.”
“Well… if a trap that flashy didn't leave you with so much as a scratch, then nothing's really scary to you, is it.”
“Shion, I understand how you feel, but try not to let it get to you too much.”
Crocodile Guy was saying something or other nonsensical. Not that it concerned me in the slightest. Itsuki looked irritated at my reply, but turned his attention back to Father once more.
“Well, about that—you know Éclair here, right? She's the one I received as a reward from our duel.”
“…Yes, that's right. The woman who became a symbol of hope for the demi-humans and beastmen within Melromarc.”
“Y-yes. I am Eclair Seaetto. And you are, I presume… the Bow Hero.”
“So then, why have you all come here?”
“Upon deciphering a message hidden within a portrait left behind in my father's will, it became clear that something was here, so we came to investigate.”
With that, Éclair and the others explained to Itsuki the circumstances that had led them here.
“I see… so it's no surprise at all that you'd end up here, of all people. Emia-san.”

“Yes. Eclair-sama, this is a hidden passage that the late Seaetto-sama left behind—one meant to let demi-humans and beastmen safely flee the country should anything ever happen within Melromarc. We were entrusted with its construction and concealment.”

“The mole with Itsuki stated that. Goodness, such an item was right here. I had no idea whatsoever. The moles from a different loop were not talking about it at all, either. However, if such a passageway exists, would it not be best to hurry and use it to escape? What is the meaning of being captured so leisurely when encountering slave hunters? No... perhaps it is an item of such caliber that if the location were identified, escape would be impossible.”

“If it were not for the fact that, in the event of an emergency, we were commanded to speak of it to no one under any circumstances save for trusted individuals like Lady Eclair... We could not allow the people of Melromarc to learn of the escape route, and our clansmen kept it hidden no matter what occurred.”
“Such an item...”
“If this existed, the people could have been protected from the slave hunts after Lord Saelgret passed away...”

Eclair and the crocodile man are making somewhat bitter expressions. Well, it is Eclair, after all. Since she summarily lynched the faction that suddenly began slave hunting, there was no way for her to know. Above all, if there was time to decipher a difficult message that must also be asked of the crocodile man, it would have been better to simply be told the location right away. I also think this because when I was back in Japan, I occasionally solved riddles with people who devised incomprehensible puzzles.
“An escape route like that is unnecessary for us right now. We shall move out of the country swiftly using portals!”
“Wah... he boldly stated the very thing we are intentionally trying to avoid mentioning...”
Eclair, the crocodile man, and Itsuki are knitting their brows unpleasantly and glaring at me for some reason, but it is the truth! Father-in-law and the others have astonished expressions.
“That is certainly true. However, it is also a fact that it could serve as an emergency escape route for those who cannot receive the protection of the heroes.”
